summary.en: Trace three elementary sorts and compare their movement, stability and cost.
summary.bn: তিনটি সর্টের ধাপ দেখো; কোনটি কত কাজ করে আর সমান মানের ক্রম রাখে কি না তুলনা করো।

notes: qsort is part of the C89 library; this lesson uses its C17 interface and C99-style loops.

sections.title: Build order through a repeated small step
Use the same array interface for three algorithms
Trace bubble, selection and insertion separately
A comparator must define a consistent order

examples.title: Bubble sort adjacent pairs
examples.explanationHtml: The largest unsorted value moves right each pass. The final line is 1 2 4 5.

examples.title: Selection sort chooses a minimum
examples.explanationHtml: The selected minima are 1, 2 and 4. Swapping each into the next slot produces 1 2 4 5.

examples.title: Insertion sort grows a sorted prefix
examples.explanationHtml: Keys 1, 4 and 2 are inserted in turn. Shifting larger values leaves space for each saved key.

examples.title: Use the standard-library sorter
examples.explanationHtml: The comparator returns negative, zero or positive using comparisons. Subtracting arbitrary ints could overflow instead.

practice.title: Bubble-sort a bounded list
practice.statementHtml: Read n from 0 to 20 and n ints from -100 to 100. Print Count and values: first, then the values in nondecreasing order separated by single spaces and a newline. Use bubble sort.
hints: Follow the bubble pass rule and preserve all original occurrences.

practice.title: Selection-sort negative scores
practice.statementHtml: Read n from 0 to 20 and n ints from -100 to 100. Print Count and values: first, then the values in nondecreasing order separated by single spaces and a newline. Use selection sort.
hints: Follow the selection pass rule and preserve all original occurrences.

practice.title: Insertion-sort a nearly ordered list
practice.statementHtml: Read n from 0 to 20 and n ints from -100 to 100. Print Count and values: first, then the values in nondecreasing order separated by single spaces and a newline. Use insertion sort.
hints: Follow the insertion pass rule and preserve all original occurrences.

practice.title: Sort and remove duplicates
practice.statementHtml: Read n from 0 to 20 and n ints from -100 to 100. Print Count and values: then distinct values in ascending order, separated by spaces and ending with a newline. Use insertion sort, followed by one scan.
hints: Only print the first entry or an entry different from its predecessor.

practice.title: Count insertion shifts
practice.statementHtml: Read n from 0 to 20 and n ints from -100 to 100. Print Count and values: then the number of element-right shifts made by insertion sort using a strict greater-than test.
hints: Increment only when copying a preceding element to the next position.

quiz.prompt: What becomes fixed after a complete left-to-right bubble pass?
options: The largest remaining value reaches the right edge
The smallest value always reaches index zero
Only the first two elements are meaningful
quiz.explanation: Adjacent swaps push the current largest value through the unsorted region.

quiz.prompt: What must selection sort find before its outer swap?
options: The minimum of the complete remaining suffix
The maximum of the sorted prefix
The median of the entire array
quiz.explanation: Scanning the whole suffix ensures the chosen entry belongs in the next prefix slot.

quiz.prompt: One bubble pass moves the largest value right. Which intermediate array appears?
quiz.explanation: The value four moves past one, three and two in three swaps, leaving one, three, two, four.

quiz.prompt: Why save the insertion key before shifting?
options: Shifts can overwrite its original array slot
quiz.explanation: The local saved value preserves the key while larger elements move right.

quiz.prompt: Which shown sorts preserve the order of equal keys?
options: Selection with an arbitrary minimum swap
Bubble and insertion with strict comparisons
quiz.explanation: The strict adjacent swaps and strict shifts do not move an equal later key before an earlier one.

quiz.prompt: The first selection pass chooses one. Which two positions are exchanged?
quiz.explanation: The minimum at index two is exchanged with the outer start at zero.

quiz.prompt: What is the worst-case time shared by these three elementary sorts?
quiz.explanation: Nested passes can make a quadratic number of comparisons or shifts.

quiz.prompt: Which sort still scans quadratically on an already sorted list here?
quiz.explanation: Selection still searches each remaining suffix; the other two have linear best cases.

quiz.prompt: How many right shifts insert one into the sorted prefix two, four, six?
quiz.explanation: Six, four and two each shift right once, so the key needs three shifts.

quiz.prompt: What does a stable sort preserve?
quiz.explanation: Equal-key records can retain their prior secondary order even while other positions change.

quiz.prompt: Why avoid return *a - *b in a general int comparator?
quiz.explanation: Use relational comparisons to obtain a safe negative, zero or positive result.

quiz.prompt: Does C require qsort to be stable or implemented as quicksort?
quiz.explanation: The standard specifies the sorting interface and comparator behavior, not those implementation properties.

quiz.prompt: Which two properties together check that a result is an ascending sort of the input?
options: Nondecreasing order and preserved occurrence counts
Only equal input and output lengths
quiz.explanation: An ordered list can still contain wrong values, so occurrence preservation is also necessary.

keyPoints.en: Bubble sort exchanges adjacent out-of-order elements.
keyPoints.bn: bubble sort পাশাপাশি ভুল ক্রমে থাকা মান বদলায়।

keyPoints.en: Selection sort places one minimum per outer pass.
keyPoints.bn: selection sort প্রতি পাসে একটি সর্বনিম্ন মান ঠিক জায়গায় রাখে।

keyPoints.en: Insertion sort inserts the next key into a sorted prefix.
keyPoints.bn: insertion sort পরের মানকে আগের সাজানো অংশে ঢোকায়।

keyPoints.en: Strict comparisons preserve equal-key order in bubble and insertion sort.
keyPoints.bn: কঠোর তুলনা ব্যবহার করলে bubble ও insertion sort-এ সমান কীর ক্রম থাকে।

keyPoints.en: All three elementary sorts have quadratic worst-case time.
keyPoints.bn: তিনটি প্রাথমিক সর্টের সবচেয়ে খারাপ ক্ষেত্রে সময় বর্গানুপাতিক।

keyPoints.en: qsort requires a consistent comparator and does not promise stability.
keyPoints.bn: qsort-এ সঙ্গত তুলনাকারী ফাংশন লাগে; সমান কীর ক্রম রাখার নিশ্চয়তা নেই।

examQuestions.question: Compare the sorted regions and stability of bubble, selection and insertion sort as implemented.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Bubble fixes a final suffix through adjacent exchanges. Selection grows a prefix by selecting suffix minima. Insertion grows a sorted prefix by inserting a saved key. Strict bubble swaps and insertion shifts preserve equal-key order. The selection swap can reverse equal-key records. All have quadratic worst-case time.

#include <stdio.h>



int main(void)
{
    int a[] = {4, 1, 3, 2};
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
        if (a[i] > a[i + 1]) {
            int t = a[i];
            a[i] = a[i + 1];
            a[i + 1] = t;
        }
    }
    printf("%d %d %d %d\n", a[0], a[1], a[2], a[3]);
    return 0;
}

1 3 2 4

The value four moves past one, three and two in three swaps, leaving one, three, two, four.

examQuestions.question: Read n from 0 to 20 and n ints from -100 to 100. Print Count and values: then the number of element-right shifts made by insertion sort using a strict greater-than test.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
#include <stdio.h>



int main(void)
{
    int n;
    int values[20];
    puts("Count and values:");
    if (scanf("%d", &n) != 1 || n < 0 || n > 20) {
        return 1;
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        if (scanf("%d", &values[i]) != 1 || values[i] < -100 || values[i] > 100) {
            return 1;
        }
    }

    int shifts = 0;
    for (int next = 1; next < n; next++) {
        int key = values[next], position = next;
        while (position > 0 && values[position - 1] > key) {
            values[position] = values[position - 1];
            position--;
            shifts++;
        }
        values[position] = key;
    }
    printf("%d\n", shifts);
    return 0;
}

Increment only when copying a preceding element to the next position.

For input 0, the program prints:

Count and values:
0

examQuestions.question: Which two properties together check that a result is an ascending sort of the input? Choose and justify: Only a nonnegative first value; Nondecreasing order and preserved occurrence counts; Only an unchanged sum; Only equal input and output lengths.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Nondecreasing order and preserved occurrence counts. An ordered list can still contain wrong values, so occurrence preservation is also necessary.
